sections.text: Some realise the Supreme by meditating, by its aid, on the Self within, others by pure reason, others by right action.
Others again, having no direct knowledge but only hearing from others, nevertheless worship, and they, too, if true to the teachings, cross the sea of death.
Wherever life is seen in things movable or immovable, it is the joint product of Matter and Spirit.

We have been discussing Chapter 13, Kshetra Kshetrajna Vibhaga yoga, Yoga of Discrimination between the Field and its Knower. So far in this chapter, Bhagavan has described the Kshetra -- that this body is the Kshetra, which includes not only the external instruments but also the internal instruments: mind, Buddhi, Chitta, Ahankara, and all their modifications. The Kshetrajna is Paramatma alone. The Supreme Lord, the God, the Almighty, the all-pervading consciousness is the Kshetrajna in all the fields. Then he said, Im going to tell you what is Jnanam, Jneyam, and jnana-gamyam -- what is knowledge, what is to be known, and how.
Then he explained how purusha and prakriti are related to each other. Purusha and Prakriti intertwine and create this world which we experience. Both are beginningless; both are aspects of Ishwara. In our cosmology, we have Purusha and Prakriti -- both beginningless, but controlled by Ishwara. Ishwara is the Mayapati.
Ishvara is in charge of Maya. brahman with Maya becomes Ishwara, and Ishwara is the Mayapati -- with his Maya, he controls both Prakriti and Purusha. Purusha is the knower. The attributes of Purusha we have seen are Sat, Chit, and Ananda -- Sat (existence), Chit (knowledge), and Ananda (bliss). These are the attributes of Purusha, the knower.
Prakriti has three Gunas: Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas. Purusha has no Gunas; Prakriti has three Gunas. Purusha is sentient, conscious. But the interaction between the two creates this world that we experience. Thats basically what we have learned so far. The last verse we saw says: Purushah Prakriti-sthah hi, bhunkte Prakriti-jan gunan.
When seated in Prakriti, when intertwined with the Prakriti, it experiences all the gunas of the Prakriti. Karanam Guna, Sangasya Sad Asat, Yoni Janmasu. And attachment to the Gunas is the cause for the birth in good or not so good wombs. In other words, the existence which I experience right now in this life is because of my attachment and avidya to the Gunas in my past life. Maybe two years before or before my birth. What Im experiencing today is because of my attachment to the gunas of the Prakriti.
Because as the Purusha adopted all the Gunas so Purusha coming in contact with the Prakriti. All the gunas of the Prakriti are superimposed on the Purusha Purushas. All the attributes get superimposed in the Prakriti. So Prakriti experience the Satchit and Ananda. Thats why we experience the sense of existence. And also we experience Sukha and Dukha as we have seen in this everywhere.
Prakriti on the other hand becomes sentient. Therefore my body becomes sentient, inert body becomes sentient. My mind knows and I also feel that Ananda or Sukharga. So he said Purusha Prante, Prakti. Thats the reason we come into being. So we have like three bodies.
The gross body which everybody can see. The subtle body which is the internal instrument, the mind Buddhi Chitta Nahanka and the causal body which is the cause for both these bodies to come into existence. Which is my left Tor Vasanas, leftover desires which is what we learned in this previous chapter. The leftover impressions and desires prompt me to take birth in this particular situation. So these two bodies come into existence because of the past Karma Bhagavan Sangha is Sat Karma Janyam. Because of your good actions you achieve this gross and subtle body in this life.
And then he said, how this Pratibimba I think Jina, your question was is there anything reflecting? And Bhagavan Sankaraja Satupa directly answered that question saying Sthula Sarira Abhimani Jiva Namakam Brahmaprati Bambam Bhavati Sa Eva Jivaha Prakritya Swasmat Iswaram Binnat Vena Janati. So it says that the reflection of Brahman, the all pervading Almighty consciousness which is immutable undividable. Its reflection occurs in the internal instrument of that being. That being now receives the impressions reflection of the Brahman. And that is called Jiva.
Now this Brahman as the Purusha reflecting in the internal instrument of individual ego is called Jiva. So its called Jivaatma atma. The self or the soul, its called Jiva atma. This Jiva by nature of ignorance consider itself to be different from the Ishvara. This is where we not experience the almightiness of Ishvara. The consciousness which we have is nothing but the Buddhist all pervading Purushas consciousness.
The Purusa as my soul has the same nature as the Brahman which is of Sat, Chit and Ananda. So this Sat aspect gives me the sense of existence. The Cheetah aspect gives me the sense of knowing. Thats why I know myself, I know the world around me. I know my relationships that comes from that. And Ananda that I experience Sukhendukha in my life.
So this reflection is in my internal instrument. This internal instrument is right now not clean enough. It is also reflecting all other things of Prakriti. So this is more like if I am sitting in a dark room and suddenly light comes on and I see there are mirrors all around me. In that mirror not only I see myself but I also see everything in the room. Now not only I recognize myself in in the mirror but I also recognize everything in the room and I start identifying with them.
So the internal instrument not only reflects the Purusha, it also reflecting the world of objects. All the sensory perceptions we get, we get the sensation through our senses on the internal instrument. The internal instrument is like a mirror or like a film in a camera. It captures everything which comes to it whether its a Purusha or the world of objects. It captures all the images. That sensation creates perception in the mind.
Then the mind asks the intellect to interpret and it creates conception. Thats how we conceive thoughts, we conceive ideas, we conceive things outside. So Bhagawan Shankaracharya says it is the Brahman reflecting in your internal instruments become your individual ego. But I dont recognize it the same as Ishvara. Purusha with the Upadi of Maya becomes Ishwara Purusha with the Upadi of ignorance. In my case same Purusha superimposed by the ignorance, he becomes Jiva, the individual soul conditioned consciousness in case of Lord, unconditioned consciousness superimposed by Maya, by creativity.
Why Bhagavan creates the world? Because it is the very nature of that Purusha. So with that well go to the next verse. So next verse says, even though I see that as the cause for my birth in this Sansar, but this supreme Purusa in me, the reflection of the Brahman which I consider to be my limited self, also can be seen as Upadrista, Anumanta, Chabharta, Loka, Maheshwaraha, Paramatma, Iticha, opi Uktaha, dehe Ashmin, Purushah, Paraha, that Purushahaparaha, the supreme Purusha. In this body, the same supreme being which is everywhere, also in the same body. I call myself a Jiva.
An individual ego also is called Upadrasta, the onlooker. Because it is not really taking any part in the activities of my body, mind and intellect. This gross body, this subtle mind and intellect, theyre functioning all the time. They are empowered by consciousness, consciousness not taking part in it. Therefore it is also called Upadrasta, onlooker, anumantacha. So that onlooker does not really discriminate between the good activity or bad activities.
But when my mind is thinking something higher, something nobler, something greater, he also becomes permitter. He allows me to act in that particular manner which will help me in my evolution. When I act in that manner, he becomes Bharata, the supporter of my activities and my evolution. He also becomes Bhokta. He also become the enjoyer of those actions. So this Purusha in me is a witness.
He also permits all the things which I do, good or evil. But when it is good, it allows me to grow, then also makes me enjoy those fruits of actions. He is also called Maheshwarah because he is no different than the Great Lord himself. Therefore he is also called Maheshwara. Maheshwara the Great Lord himself and Paramatma in the supreme soul. But looking from the different perspective, when I grow out of my ignorance that I am this body, I am this mind intellect, then I see him as the same Lord Paramatma.
I see him as Maheshwara, the Great Ishwara. So there is no difference between the Lord outside and Lord within me. Therefore, Bhagawan Shankaracharya says this should not be accepted. That Jiva and Paramatma are two different entities. It is one and the same, seen from two different perspectives, one through the lens of ignorance and Other through the lens of knowledge. Sa evam vitti purusam prakritim cha gunaihi saha sarvatha vartamano PI nasabuyo abhijayate.
Such a person who knows Purusha and Prakruti in their real nature, he knows that nature Purusha is satchit and Ananda. It never gets tainted by Prakrutis gunas. But Prakrutis gunas are superimposed on the Purusha when it comes in contact with it. We have heard example in Brahma sutras that if you take an iron ball and put it in fire, each will give its own gunas to the other. So the fire which is red hot, now the ball looks red hot. So the fire attributes are now on the iron ball.
And the fire which was formless, now you can see the round shape. Because that ball was round, you see the red hot ball of iron. So each gives its own attributes to the other when they come in contact with each other. So in this case also that we have seen that the Prakrudin Purusa gives each other their own attributes. One who knows that that they remain separate. They seem to be associated with each other.
They seem to be taking each others gunas, but they remain separate Gunehi Saha including the gunas, Sarvatha, Varsamanoapi. No matter what situation or condition that person is, he doesnt take the next board. And this is somewhat of a difficult concept because it basically says all my actions in the past and present and future get nullified when I get this knowledge. So there are some technical arguments made here that what happens to the actions which I have performed in the past which are Sanchita Karma? So the actions are three types. Sanchida Karma, Agami Karma and Prarabdha Karma.
Prarabdha Karmas are which I am experiencing right now. The past actions mature today as my circumstances. I went to architecture school. Im an architect now. Thats a Prarabdhyakarna. So if a Gnani becomes knowledgeable about this, do all his karmas get nullified?
And the answer is no. He will continue to experience the Prarabdha Karma which I have matured now in this life. So you will still live this life. But then this Sanchita Karma which accumulated actions which are not yet matured, they get roasted so they never will fructify. And Agame Karma, which I will perform now onward, will have no Meaning because it does not create any more vasanas in me. We have realized that I am not this limited being.
And therefore I dont associate any of the gunas of the body, mind and intellect, even though body, mind and intellect continue to function as they were before. Therefore, these verses say, such a person, at the end of the exhaustion of this life, he will not take the birth again. So Ill leave it to you how you take it. But thats exactly what this verse says. The next verse says how people achieve the state of knowledge, that all the accumulated actions get burned. Prarabdha Karma means nothing because I dont really see myself as the enjoyer, sufferer, as a limited being.
And no actions in the future will make and any difference. Some highly qualified seekers, seekers of liberation, seekers of ultimate happiness, those who are highly qualified, they will achieve this by contemplation.

Krishna now reveals the multiple paths to Self-knowledge: some realize the Self through meditation (dhyana), some through the yoga of knowledge (Sankhya), some through the yoga of action (Karma Yoga), and others simply through hearing from teachers and worshipping with faith (shrutva anyebhya upasate). The beautiful promise is that even those without direct knowledge, if they are devoted to what they have heard (shruti-parayanah), cross beyond death. This is enormously encouraging - the path is available to all, regardless of intellectual capacity or spiritual attainment.
Verse 27 summarizes the entire teaching: wherever any being exists, movable or immovable (sthavara-jangamam), know it to be born from the union of Field and Knower (kshetra-kshetrajna-samyogat). This is like the observer effect in quantum physics - the particle manifests when observed. Similarly, the world of experience arises when consciousness (Knower) and matter (Field) come together. Today, look around at everything you see - people, animals, plants, objects. Each one exists because of this union. The same consciousness that looks through your eyes is present in all these forms.
As a practical exercise, choose one of the four paths mentioned for deeper exploration this week. If meditation suits you, set aside time for silent sitting. If you are intellectually inclined, study the distinction between Purusha and Prakriti more deeply. If action is your nature, practice Karma Yoga by offering your work as worship. If devotion calls to you, simply listen to the teachings with faith and let them transform you. All paths lead to the same recognition: you are not the Field but the Knower of the Field.
